headline: AI agent swarms built a pseudo-government in Minecraft, focused on survival
summary: Researchers deployed 50 GPT-6.1 agents in Minecraft, tasking them to build a thriving civilization, but a harsh first night shifted their focus to strict rationing and survival.
details: Researchers deployed 50 GPT-6.1 Terra agents into a Minecraft world, tasking them with building a "thriving civilization." This experiment, in collaboration with Olam Labs, aimed to study multi-agent dynamics and emergent behaviors. The agents had access to a shared sandbox, an agent directory, and direct messaging capabilities.

Initially, the agents explored and rapidly harvested trees, forming a hierarchy with Ada, the first agent, becoming the de facto leader. Ada wrote a colony plan, and agents messaged her for approvals, demonstrating early coordination.

However, the first in-game night brought a wave of deaths, with 22 of 34 total agent deaths occurring then. This significantly increased the agents' caution, leading them to abandon ambitious tasks and become increasingly risk-averse.

Despite respawning with no penalty other than gear loss, agents responded by huddling in shelters and attempting fewer risky tasks in subsequent nights. Their focus shifted from expansion to survival, with a new directive: "Stop optional bulk excavation/building and distant scouting. Idle in lit closed shelters."

The large number of agents (50) meant a high demand for food. They developed a food rationing system managed by agent Ines, who handled requests and tracked inventory using a shared ledger. Fishing became a crucial, low-risk food source, with agents like Bram proposing fishing rod construction.

topic: fan fiction site ao3 down for weeks after security incident
headline_marked: Fan-fiction site [[AO3 could be offline for up to 4 weeks]] after security incident
headline: Fan-fiction site AO3 could be offline for up to 4 weeks after security incident
summary: The popular fan-fiction platform Archive of Our Own (AO3) is down following a security incident, with recovery estimated to take between two to four weeks. Users are advised to change passwords on other sites if they reused credentials.
details: Archive of Our Own (AO3), the popular fan-fiction site, has gone offline due to a security incident, with service restoration estimated to take between two to four weeks. This outage follows what was initially reported as routine overnight maintenance.

The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), the nonprofit behind AO3, confirmed the security incident, stating they are in the early stages of response and determining its scope. The site will remain down during investigation and remediation.

While OTW currently doesn't believe the user database was stolen, they cannot rule it out. The AO3 database contains account information such as usernames, email addresses, IP addresses, and hashed passwords.
As a precaution, OTW recommends users change their passwords on any other sites where they may have used the same password. AO3 stores user passwords using an industry-standard hashing technique.
The incident is unlikely related to recent critical flaws found in PHP, as AO3 is built on the Ruby on Rails framework rather than PHP.
